message.content: {"caption":"A two-panel figure showing a branching archive of coding agents and their SWE-bench scores over successive iterations.","description":"Left: A top-down archive tree has a single circular root branching through many gray connecting lines to circular agent nodes. The lines connect parent and descendant nodes; they have no visible arrowheads or labels. Node fill color encodes SWE-bench score on the adjacent 0–0.5 scale, from dark low scores to yellow high scores. Border color encodes evaluation-task count: red denotes 10 tasks (no basic functionality), yellow denotes 60 tasks, and green denotes 200 tasks, with the legend also specifying a score threshold of at least 0.4 and a top-two-in-the-archive criterion. An outlined star marks the final best agent near the bottom of the tree. Right: A line chart plots Iterations on the x-axis (ticks 0–80 by 10) and SWE-bench Score on the y-axis (visible ticks 0.20–0.50, with the plotted range extending to about 0.15). The cyan Average of Archive series rises gradually from about 0.20 to 0.27. The blue Best Agent series is nondecreasing: it starts near 0.20, steps to about 0.25, then 0.41, 0.43, and finally 0.50, remaining level between gains. The dark Lineage to Final Best Agent series is more variable: it falls from about 0.20 to a low near 0.17 early on, rises through about 0.22 and 0.41 to about 0.43, dips to about 0.40, then rises to 0.50 near iteration 63; it is not shown continuing afterward. Gray callouts identify changes along the plotted progress: “Non-empty patch validation and retry” near the early 0.25 level; “More granular file viewing via lines” near 0.22; “More granular file editing via string replacement” near 0.41; “Auto-summarize on context limit” near 0.43; “Multiple patch generations and ranking” near the later dip around 0.40; and “History-aware patch generations and ranking” near the rise to 0.50.
